subject: Intermittent 503s affecting inference — SurgeWell: status page update & next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: support@surgewell.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-29T01:18:00Z
Subject: Intermittent 503s affecting inference — SurgeWell

Hi Alex / SurgeWell team,

We wanted to make you aware we’re investigating intermittent 503 responses from the hosted inference API that started at ~01:12 UTC and have been impacting some /v1/generate traffic. We’ve posted a short incident notice on our status page (link below) and I wanted to loop you in and ask about impact on your side.

What we know so far:
- Window: ~01:12 — ongoing at time of writing
- Symptom: HTTP 503 returned from gateway, some requests retried and queued; not all regions affected
- Affected endpoint: /v1/generate (SurgeWell tenant routed to shared pool)
- Short-term mitigation underway: routing adjustments to bypass a candidate autoscale group

Actions we’re taking now:
- On-call engineering is collecting traces and error samples (attaching a short status snapshot).
- We’re temporarily shifting traffic for high-error customers to a warmer dedicated pool while we identify root cause.
- I’ll send a follow-up update within 30–45 minutes with more detail and an ETA for full restoration.

Could you confirm whether you’re seeing increased failures on your end (error rate, specific jobs impacted, any alerts triggered)? Any sample request IDs or timestamps you can share will help correlate.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this directly affects your pipelines and appreciate the quick signal.

Status link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-04-29-intermittent-503s

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Moreno <ops@surgewell.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-29T01:32:00Z
Subject: Re: Intermittent 503s affecting inference — SurgeWell

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the heads up — we are seeing the failures. Quick notes from our side:
- Start: ~01:15 UTC; spike of errors lasted roughly 20–25 minutes, then intermittent again
- Failure mode: 503 / gateway timeout for synchronous generate calls; we also saw our retry storm cause downstream queueing for batch ingestion
- Estimated impact: ~8–12% of calls failed during the peak; several internal jobs timed out and retried
- Example IDs: req_20260429_01_1567, req_20260429_01_2079 (timestamps included in attached logs)

We’ve paused a few non-critical jobs and will keep an eye on the rate. Any ETA? If you’re planning reroutes or rollbacks, let us know if we should throttle retries on our side to avoid compounding the issue.

Attached: sample-error-log-ops.txt

– Alex
Alex Moreno
Ops Lead, SurgeWell
ops@surgewell.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-29T01:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Intermittent 503s — internal update

Naomi / team — quick internal update (cc’ing CS).

Summary of findings so far:
- Root cause (suspected): a recent autoscaler tweak caused a small subset of requests to be routed to nodes with an outdated kernel extension that rejects connections under short-burst load; that caused gateway-level 503s while the pool warmed up.
- Evidence: correlation of request IDs from SurgeWell logs with trace ids showing backend 503 at the gateway layer (samples attached to the incident record).
- Mitigation applied: rolled back the autoscale policy and forcibly reallocated affected nodes at 01:39 UTC; started traffic-shift to a warm dedicated pool for impacted tenants. Error rate dropped to baseline by ~01:52 UTC for most customers.

Next steps:
- Complete a full node sweep to eliminate any remaining contaminated kernels (ETA ~45 minutes).
- Prepare an interim postmortem and a proposed permanent fix to autoscaler policy to prevent warmup routing during bursty workloads.
- Recommend we offer SurgeWell a sympathetic credit and an invite to the deeper postmortem once it’s ready.

Please update SurgeWell (Naomi) with the rollback details and the current ETA. Aisha, can you flag this for CS outreach and coordinate credit/compensation options with Marissa?

Jonas
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-04-29T02:05:00Z
Subject: Incident follow-up: restoration & next steps (SurgeWell)

Hi Alex — quick follow-up with what we’ve completed and next steps.

Status now:
- Traffic restored to baseline for your tenant by ~01:52 UTC; no active 503s observed in the last 10 minutes when we last sampled.
- Root cause: autoscaler policy change routed traffic to partly warmed nodes running an incompatible kernel extension; when the pool warmed fully the errors subsided.

What we did for SurgeWell:
- Immediately shifted your production traffic to a warm dedicated pool to minimize retries and queueing impacts.
- Rolled back the autoscale policy that introduced the faulty warm-up behavior.
- Initiated a full node sweep and will replace any nodes with the faulty kernel.

Next steps and timeline:
- Postmortem draft: we expect a formal postmortem within 72 hours. Link to the draft: https://redwood.app/notes/incident/2026-04-29-surgewell-draft
- Remediation plan: permanent autoscaler fix and improved warm-up checks (target: deploy within 2 weeks).
- Compensation: we’d like to offer a one-time account credit for the impact window; Marissa will follow up with options.

If you’d like a short sync today to walk through the timeline and logs, we can make time — otherwise we’ll share the final postmortem when complete.

Again, apologies for the disruption and thanks for the quick logs — they helped shorten triage.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai
